synopsis: Chapter 6 presents FID, alongside KID, as a distribution-level image- or field-similarity metric for sensor-model validation [f4803]. The 2024 Instance Performance Difference paper warns that FID does not target any specific perception algorithm, a limitation also recorded in the glossary [f4819, f14796]. Whether FID, Chamfer distance or DCD predict safety-relevant perception errors remains uncertain, so the corpus does not establish FID similarity as evidence of safety-relevant perception performance [f5067].

relations.note: Both report the 2024 paper’s warning that FID targets no specific perception algorithm.
Algorithm-independent scope supports uncertainty about predicting safety-relevant perception errors.
Adds an algorithm-specificity limitation to FID’s distribution-level validation role.
